title: Left injectivity in Jacobi-Zariski for an ind-etale final map
statement: Let $A\to B\xrightarrow{\varphi}C$ be homomorphisms of commutative rings, with $B\to C$ ind-etale [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra]. Let $\mathrm{NL}_{B/A}=[I/I^2\xrightarrow{\delta}\bigoplus_{b\in B}B\,\mathrm d[b]]$, where $I=\ker(A[B]\to B)$, be the standard naive cotangent complex [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map]. Tensor this complex termwise over $B$ with $C$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], and define $H^{-1}$ to be the kernel of its differential. Let $J=\ker(A[C]\to C)$ and let $\varphi_\sharp:A[B]\to A[C]$ send $[b]$ to $[\varphi(b)]$ and fix $A$. The canonical map on conormal modules $I/I^2\otimes_B C\to J/J^2$, $[g]\otimes c\mapsto c[\varphi_\sharp(g)]$, restricts to an injective $C$-linear map $$H^{-1}(\mathrm{NL}_{B/A}\otimes_B C)\longrightarrow H^{-1}(\mathrm{NL}_{C/A}).$$ No locality, Noetherian or finite-presentation hypothesis on $A\to B$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 07D5 (lemma-transitive-colimit-lci-at-end), left-injectivity consequence for a filtered colimit of etale B-algebras; etale algebras are standard smooth by algebra.tex Tag 00U9 (lemma-etale-standard-smooth), hence local complete intersections, as explicitly used in lemma-henselization-NL.

proof.text: Choose a small filtered diagram of finitely presented etale $B$-algebras $C_i$ with colimit $C$, as in the definition of ind-etale. All rings and the index category are taken in one containing universe. By the etale ring/affine criterion and the syntomic input lemma, each $B\to C_i$ is syntomic. Choose a finite polynomial presentation $\beta_i:B[y_1,\ldots,y_{m_i}]\twoheadrightarrow C_i$. The syntomic-kernel lemma says that $\ker\beta_i$ is locally generated by Koszul-regular sequences. This applies without any condition on $A\to B$.

source.place: Tag 07D5 (lemma-transitive-colimit-lci-at-end), applied to the etale stages, as in lemma-henselization-NL; finite-stage input is Tag 07D3.

proof.text: Fix $i$, put $P=A[B]$, and form $T=P[y_1,\ldots,y_{m_i}]$. Let $q:T\twoheadrightarrow B[y_1,\ldots,y_{m_i}]$ evaluate the $[b]$ variables and fix the $y$ variables. Put $L=\ker q$ and $K=\ker(\beta_i q)$. Thus $L\subseteq K$, $T/L\cong B[y_1,\ldots,y_{m_i}]$, and $K/L$ corresponds to $\ker\beta_i$. Step 1 verifies precisely the local Koszul hypothesis of the intersection lemma, giving $L\cap K^2=LK$. The composed-conormal lemma now gives an injection $a_i:(I/I^2)\otimes_B C_i\hookrightarrow K/K^2$, $[g]\otimes c\mapsto c[g]$, reversing its tensor factors. Presentation functoriality gives the commuting differential square: for a polynomial $g\in I$, the differential of its image is the image of $\mathrm dg$; coefficients are extended to $C_i$. By linearity the square holds on every tensor. Hence $a_i$ restricts to an injection from $Z_i=\ker(\delta_{B/A}\otimes_B C_i)$ to $\ker(K/K^2\to C_i\otimes_T\Omega_{T/A})$.

source.place: Tag 07D4 (lemma-transitive-lci-at-end), proof: the intersection identity and resulting conormal injection.

proof.text: Let $P_i=A[C_i]\twoheadrightarrow C_i$ be the canonical presentation. Map $T\to P_i$ by $[b]\mapsto[\varphi_i(b)]$ and $y_j\mapsto[\beta_i(y_j)]$, fixing $A$, where $\varphi_i:B\to C_i$ is the structure map. Evaluation commutes on these generators. The presentation homotopy-equivalence lemma therefore identifies the two differential kernels over $C_i$. Indeed its identities $1-\psi_1\theta_1=h\delta$ and $1-\theta_1\psi_1=h'\delta'$ restrict to inverse identities on kernels. Compose this isomorphism with the injection of step 2 to get an injection $u_i:Z_i\to H^{-1}(\mathrm{NL}_{C_i/A})$. Its ambient conormal formula is $[g]\otimes c\mapsto c[\varphi_{i,\sharp}(g)]$, since the composite $P\to T\to P_i$ sends every $[b]$ to $[\varphi_i(b)]$. For a transition $v:C_i\to C_j$, both resulting composites on a pure tensor are $v(c)[\operatorname{rename}(v\varphi_i)(g)]$; linearity extends the equality to all tensors. Thus these injections commute with the canonical transition maps on the kernels.

source.place: Tags 07D4 and 07D5, canonical-presentation identification via algebra.tex Tag 00S1 (lemma-NL-homotopy).

proof.text: Write $Z=\ker(\delta_{B/A}\otimes_B C)$. Presentation functoriality makes the stated conormal map restrict to $u:Z\to H^{-1}(\mathrm{NL}_{C/A})$, with the same formula as in step 3. Suppose $x\in Z$ and $u(x)=0$. Apply the tensor-colimit elementwise lemma with $R=B$ and $N=I/I^2$ (using tensor symmetry) to represent $x$ by $t_i\in(I/I^2)\otimes_B C_i$. Its differential has zero image in $(\bigoplus_{b\in B}B\,\mathrm d[b])\otimes_B C$. Apply the eventual-zero clause of the same lemma with $N=\bigoplus_{b\in B}B\,\mathrm d[b]$ to advance along an arrow $i\to j$ so that the image $t_j$ is a cycle, hence lies in $Z_j$. The canonical image of $u_j(t_j)$ is $u(x)=0$, by the formula in step 3. Apply the canonical cotangent-colimit comparison with base $A$ and diagram $(C_i)$, writing $K$ for its degreewise colimit complex. Its colimit hypothesis holds: the index category is filtered, hence connected, so the colimit cocone $(C,\iota_i)$ of $B$-algebras is computed on underlying commutative rings and is also a colimit cocone of commutative $A$-algebras, the transition maps being $B$-, hence $A$-algebra maps. The image $z$ of $u_j(t_j)$ in $K^{-1}$ is a cycle, and its image in $H^{-1}(\mathrm{NL}_{C/A})$ is zero. The comparison is a quasi-isomorphism, so $[z]=0$ in $H^{-1}(K)$. Since $K^{-2}=0$, there are no boundaries in degree $-1$, hence $z=0$ in $K^{-1}$. This module is by construction the colimit of the canonical conormal modules. The module-colimit elementwise lemma gives an arrow $j\to k$ killing $u_j(t_j)$ already in that conormal module, hence in its differential kernel. Compatibility from step 3 says $u_k(t_k)=0$. Since $u_k$ is injective, $t_k=0$, and its image $x$ is zero. The canonical map is $C$-linear, so zero kernel proves its injectivity. No transition injectivity or flatness of $C$ over a stage was used.
